heading: INT. LIGHTHOUSE LAMP ROOM TEA SHOP - DUSK

units.text: INT. LIGHTHOUSE LAMP ROOM TEA SHOP - DUSK
The lamp room of a decommissioned lighthouse, glazed on all sides, the great lens long ago swapped for six mismatched tables.
Salt has frosted the windows from outside.
Inside, steam from a copper urn beads on the brass rail.
Every cup in the room is chipped in the same place, as if by one clumsy hand.
ODALYS VANCE, forties, a insurance assessor in a rain-spotted camel coat, sits with her back to the sea.
Her notebook is closed.
Her pen is not.
BRAM OKONKWO, sixties, the shop's owner, a broad man with flour-white forearms and a limp he pretends is a stroll, sets a teapot between them without being asked.
HESTER PELL, eighties, sits at the farthest table in a knitted hat, spooning sugar into a cup that is already full.
She has not looked up since Odalys arrived.
The policy was taken out eleven days before the fire.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: Eleven days is a good number. Lucky, in some places.
units.name: BRAM

units.text: The fire started in the cellar. The cellar had no wiring. No stove. Nothing that burns by itself.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: Old buildings do surprise us.
units.name: BRAM

units.text: Your lease says the cellar was sealed in 1994. Someone unsealed it. Someone with a key to a door that, on paper, does not exist.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: I have a great many keys. Lighthouses are sentimental about keys.
units.name: BRAM

units.text: Mr. Okonkwo, I am not accusing you.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: That is the most frightening sentence in your language.
units.name: BRAM

units.text: He did not light it.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: Mrs. Pell. I did not know you were listening.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: I have listened to this room for fifty years. It is the only thing I do properly.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: Hester, please.
units.name: BRAM

units.text: Your father kept the lamp, Bram. Mine kept the logbook. You know what a logbook is for.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: Not now.
units.name: BRAM

units.text: What is it for, Mrs. Pell?
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: For the nights nobody wants remembered.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: That book burned.
units.name: BRAM

units.text: That book is in my handbag.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: Then the fire was not an accident, and it was not for the insurance.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: Stop. Both of you. Stop talking.
units.name: BRAM

units.text: He wrote a name on page forty. A boy. Seventeen. The wrong rocks, the right storm. Your father let the lamp go dark that night, Bram, to save oil.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: He was ordered to.
units.name: BRAM

units.text: He was paid to.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: And the cellar?
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: The cellar is where the boy was kept until the tide went out.
units.name: HESTER

units.text: The urn hisses.
Bram's hand closes on the teapot handle and the pot shatters against the brass rail, tea running black across the floorboards toward Hester's shoes.
Nobody was meant to ever open that door!
units.name: BRAM
